items.title: Albert "Baby Brousse" Broussard Interview, 1961-02-20
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] You talk about Big Bill's brother? Big Bill's brother. [INTERVIEWEE] Oh, yeah.

ctx.x: Yeah, Carbone. We used to call him Kev. Frank Carbone. It was a nickname that we gave him. His name was Frank Thomas, see? But we called him Frank Carbone. Oh, yeah.
You talk about Big Bill's brother? Big Bill's brother.

items.title: Albert "Baby Brousse" Broussard Interview, 1961-02-20
items.q: And that was fellas like Newman, Udell, Big Bill Thompson, myself.

ctx.x: The shardest, he played, tell you how he played waltzes.

And that's what I was fixing to say. The waltz and the shardest, that was a popular dance. They contest you on the shardest. Oh, yeah? Yeah. You dance around right and left. You never stop turning. You go all the way to the other hall, and you keep turning. You never give up action. And the same way with the piano. The guy played the piano. He never let up on the beat of the number. The shardest was a hard number all the way for dancing and playing. Very few piano players played the shardest. There was only about…
Udell, what was his last name?
